update: Joseph's office reviewed the carrier appraiser's estimate on July 28 and sent back a list of additional items that should be included; the file is now in appraiser-to-appraiser negotiation over scope before Joseph issues his own position.

timeline.event: Contractor submitted the file and requested Joseph pursue the appraisal for the homeowner.
Office sent the appraisal demand letter to the homeowner.
Office sent a draft estimate to the contractor for review.
Contractor approved the draft estimate; the demand package was sent to Allstate to formally invoke appraisal.
Homeowner reported Allstate's own adjuster reinspected and again found no roof damage.
Allstate sent its adjuster's estimate on the claim.
Homeowner confirmed she wanted to continue with the appraisal; office re-sent the file to Allstate.
Allstate's administrator named Robert Thomas as the carrier's appraiser and an inspection was scheduled.
Carrier's appraiser agreed to the proposed umpire and requested a signed appraisal agreement.
Appraisal agreement was signed and exchanged with the carrier's appraiser.
Carrier's appraiser held his inspection of the property.
Carrier's appraiser sent his position/estimate.
Joseph reviewed the carrier's estimate and sent back additional items to include.

update: The demand package was sent to Farmers Insurance to formally invoke appraisal on May 21, and Farmers posted a new appraisal-related claim document to the portal on June 4; no carrier appraiser assignment or position has come through by email since then.

timeline.event: Contractor requested an appraisal demand letter and outlined the scope of work needed (roof, two metal sheds, fence, playground, and a shingle shed).
Office sent the appraisal demand letter to the homeowner; contractor supplied photos of the damage.
Homeowner signed the appraisal demand letter.
Office sent the draft estimate to the contractor, who approved it.
Office sent the demand package to Farmers Insurance to formally invoke appraisal; homeowner confirmed receipt.
Farmers Insurance posted a new appraisal-related claim document to the online claim portal.

update: Joseph's office reviewed the carrier appraiser's position on August 1 and asked him to add several specific scope items; the carrier's appraiser has floated moving to umpire if the two sides cannot agree.

timeline.event: The public adjuster formally invoked appraisal on the homeowner's behalf and named Joseph as the appraiser.
The carrier's appraiser reached out to coordinate umpire selection and scheduling.
The public adjuster sent the estimate and claim file to Joseph's office; office offered a solo inspection date to the carrier's appraiser.
The carrier confirmed the claim is officially in appraisal and both appraisers were formally designated.
Inspection planned for 5/21 was postponed due to a rain forecast.
Inspection was rescheduled and confirmed with the homeowner for June 2.
Inspection was held; Joseph's inspector found interior ceiling damage but noted the roof itself had already been replaced by the homeowner.
Office agreed to a proposed umpire candidate.
Carrier's appraiser followed up asking for photos of the roof from before the homeowner's replacement.
Requested pre-replacement roof photos were sent to the carrier's appraiser.
Carrier's appraiser sent his position/estimate and suggested moving to umpire if no agreement is reached.
Joseph's office reviewed the estimate and requested that several specific scope items be added.

update: As of today, Joseph's office and the carrier's appraiser have agreed on the remaining scope items (splash guards and overhead & profit); the file is moving toward a final agreed estimate rather than needing an umpire.

timeline.event: The contractor's public adjuster (Cross Country Public Adjusting) shared the claim file with Joseph's office.
Foremost Insurance posted a new appraisal-related claim document to its portal.
Carrier's appraiser reached out with the appraiser designation and offered a solo inspection date.
Office sent the inspection schedule to the homeowner.
Homeowner confirmed the inspection date with interior access.
Carrier's appraiser corrected the inspection date; office rescheduled and the homeowner reconfirmed.
Office sent requested documents to the carrier's appraiser following the inspection.
Carrier's appraiser sent his draft estimate for review.
Office reviewed the draft and requested several additional items be included.
Carrier's appraiser agreed to some items and pushed back on one item.
Office agreed to the carrier appraiser's terms, moving the file toward a final agreed estimate.
